title: Clonal articular cartilage progenitors outperform mesenchymal stromal cells in mitigating post-traumatic osteoarthritis.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to compare the functional, pathological, and immunomodulatory properties of articular chondroprogenitors (ACPs) with those of bone-marrow-derived mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs) in preventing the progression of post-traumatic osteoarthritis (PTOA) after destabilization of the medial meniscus (DMM) injury in a mouse model.
METHOD: ACP and MSC were isolated from three horses and assessed for their immunomodulatory capacity in vitro. Aliquots of selected ACP clones and MSCs were injected intra-articularly into male mice 1-week post destabilization of the medial meniscus (DMM). The functional mobility of the mice before the injury and at weeks 2, 4, and 8 post-injury was assessed by two methods: ANY-maze™ voluntary mobility monitoring and DigiGait™ compulsory gait analysis. Upon euthanasia, joints were collected for histological scoring.
RESULTS: In vitro assessments demonstrated that ACPs and MSCs had anti-inflammatory properties: both treatments produced lower levels of pro-inflammatory cytokines, while only the ACPs produced more anti-inflammatory cytokines than controls. In vivo, both ACPs and MSCs lessened the effects of DMM on mobility. Histological scoring revealed significant reductions of PTOA in the medial compartment with ACPs relative to both MSCs and vehicle controls. Overall, ACPs effectively reduced PTOA progression to a greater extent than MSCs.
CONCLUSION: Our findings demonstrated that both equine ACP and MSC treatments provided symptom modification over vehicle controls in a short-term animal study. Notably, ACPs may be more efficacious than MSCs at reducing structural joint pathology.

title: Multidimensional Pre-Competition Stress Profiles in Wheelchair Basketball: Associations with Cortisol and Psychological Indicators.
abstract: This study examined pre-competition cortisol levels and psychological anticipation in wheelchair basketball athletes using a person-centred approach. Thirty-four male athletes (mean age: 35 ± 7.75 years) competing in a regional league provided saliva samples 35-50 min before competition and completed psychological assessments with the Revised Competitive State Anxiety Inventory-2 (CSAI-2R) and the Perceived Stress Scale. K-Means cluster analysis (k = 3), validated by Ward's hierarchical clustering (ARI = 0.947; NMI = 0.892) and Bootstrap Jaccard stability (0.544-0.603), identified three exploratory stress profiles: Low Reactor (n = 5; low cortisol, anxiety, and stress), High Reactor (n = 20; moderate cortisol, high cognitive/physical anxiety), and Physiological Stress Reactor (n = 9; high cortisol, high stress, moderate anxiety). Significant group differences were observed for log(Cortisol) (H(2) = 17.095, p < 0.001, ε2 = 0.518), Cognitive Anxiety (H(2) = 13.900, p < 0.01, ε2 = 0.421), Somatic Anxiety (H(2) = 18.840, p < 0.001, ε2 = 0.571), and Perceived Stress (H(2) = 21.831, p < 0.001, ε2 = 0.662), while self-confidence did not differ. Exploratory logistic regression indicated that functional classification, years of sport participation, match location, and match result did not significantly predict the Physiological Stress Reactor membership. These findings suggest that pre-competition stress-related characteristics may manifest in different combinations of physiological and psychological indicators. The identified profiles should be considered exploratory and require validation in larger and independent samples.

title: Long-Term Fitness Profile and Performance-Related Indicators in Semi-Professional Female Handball Players.
abstract: Long-term, single-club datasets linking fitness and match performance are rare in women's handball. This retrospective study profiled fitness and game-quality indicators across 14 seasons (2010-2022, 2026; N = 45; 8-17 players/season). Anthropometric and specific-fitness values (height 173.90 ± 5.53 cm, body mass 68.28 ± 8.08 kg, jump-throw velocity 79.94 ± 6.83 km/h, countermovement jump 43.46 ± 4.84 cm, VO2max 48.01 ± 3.61 mL/kg/min) were sub-elite. Shot efficiency (55.74 ± 6.00%) approached elite values (58.90 ± 7.60%). Backs were older, more experienced, and higher-scoring than Wings and Pivots. Universal players matched Backs' output despite being younger and less experienced. Experience correlated with goals per match (r = 0.51, p = 0.001), positive actions (r = 0.44, p = 0.005), and action balance (r = 0.47, p = 0.003). Throwing velocity and sprint/agility speed showed similar associations. Endurance, strength, and coordination/dribble deficit showed none. Fitness indicators improved across 2010-2022, but a single season after near-complete roster turnover departed markedly from this trend. Trends should not be extrapolated to a changed roster without retesting. A small set of trainable, sport-specific qualities, not general fitness, best predicts match performance. Findings provide normative benchmarks and training priorities for coaches.

title: Effect of Repeat Deceleration on Countermovement Jump and Kicking Performance in Male and Female Football Players.
abstract: Wei, X, Zhu, H, Zheng, X, Gao, Y, Huang, J, Chen, X, Vigh-Larsen, JF, Mohr, M, and Krustrup, P. Greater reductions in deceleration compared with sprint ability following repeated high-intensity exercise in male and female soccer players, but no effect on countermovement jump (CMJ) or ball-kicking performance. J Strength Cond Res XX(X): 000-000, 2026-The aim of this study was to examine the acute effect of repeated sprint and deceleration on the fatigue of each component (sprint vs. deceleration) and on CMJ and soccer kicking performance, and to investigate the association between deceleration ability and fatigue. Thirty-three high-level male (n = 18) and female (n = 15) college soccer players completed 10 × 15-m sprints with subsequent 5-m enforced deceleration, interspersed with 20-s recovery intervals. Sprint and deceleration performance were measured continuously during the protocol, while CMJ and kicking performance were assessed before and immediately after. Furthermore, the players' deceleration ability was measured using deceleration deficit and deceleration index. Peak deceleration had significantly higher fatigue index (FI) and decrement score (Sdec) compared with speed (p < 0.05, Cohen's d = 3.18-3.32), while no significant decline was found in CMJ or kicking performance after the repeated sprint and deceleration protocol (p > 0.05, Cohen's d = -0.06∼0.23). A significant repeated sprint and deceleration × sex interaction effect was observed in peak ball speed (p < 0.05, ηp2 = 0.149), with women showing a decrease in peak ball speed compared with their male counterparts. The deceleration index correlated with FI and Sdec of speed (r = -0.444∼-0.516, p < 0.05), and the rate of CMJ decline correlated with FI and Sdec deceleration (r = 0.530-0.549, p < 0.05). Finally, the rate of decline in kicking speed was positively correlated with the Sdec deceleration rate (r = 0.423, p < 0.05). Deceleration capacity is more prone to acute fatigue than sprint ability. In addition, repeated sprint and deceleration had a limited effect on athletic performance, but men and women showed different adjusted trends in kicking speed. Finally, players having better deceleration capacity show a smaller performance drop.

title: Countermovement Jump Performance Across Ten Competitive Microcycles in Under-18 Soccer Players: An Analysis of Delayed and Long-Term Responses to Training and Official Competition.
abstract: Villaseca-Vicuña, R, Freitas, TT, Spyrou, K, Marín-Cascales, E, Comyns, T, Loturco, I, and Zabaloy, S. Countermovement jump performance across 10 competitive microcycles in under-18 soccer players: An analysis of delayed and long-term responses to training and official competition. J Strength Cond Res XX(X): 000-000, 2026-The aims of this study were to (a) determine within-microcycle changes in countermovement jump (CMJ) measures (i.e., jump height, reactive strength index modified [RSImod], and eccentric peak velocity [EPV]) collected 2 days after (MD+2) and 1 day before (MD-1) the match-day across 10 weeks during the competitive period in under-18 soccer players and (b) analyze week-to-week variations in the selected CMJ-metrics collected on MD+2 across the entire mesocycle. Twelve (n = 12) under-18 academy soccer players (age: 17.5 ± 0.5 years; body mass: 71.9 ± 7.7 kg) volunteered to participate in this study. Over 10 competitive weeks, CMJ assessments were recorded on force plates at 2 key microcycle time points: MD+2 (active recovery phase at the start of the microcycle) and MD-1 (end of the microcycle). Results showed significant within-week changes in CMJ height and EPV in most of the training microcycles (p: <0.001 to 0.049) while RSImod showed significant changes in only 4 of the 10 microcycles (p: 0.001 to 0.049). Similarly, the between-week comparisons showed significant variations only in EPV and RSI (p: 0.005 to 0.049). These findings suggest that jump height might be better suited to assess within-week changes, while RSImod appears to hold greater discriminative value for detecting between-week fluctuations. Eccentric peak velocity, in turn, may provide useful information for both within-week and between-week changes in young soccer players.

title: All-Inside Posterior Cruciate Ligament Reconstruction Using Achilles Allograft and Suture Tape Augmentation.
abstract: Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL) reconstruction is challenged by graft elongation and delayed biological integration, often necessitating slow rehabilitation and carrying a risk of arthrofibrosis. This technical report describes an all-inside technique augmented with the modified internal bracing to address these limitations. The technique involves integrating a FiberTape within a quadrupled Achilles tendon allograft, creating a load-sharing composite. An all-inside, retrograde socket method was used for anatomic PCL reconstruction in the knee, with suspensory fixation on both femur and tibia. The graft-tape construct was simultaneously tensioned. The technique provides immediate biomechanical stability by mitigating graft micromotion, elongation, and tunnel abrasion. By closely replicating native PCL stiffness, this construct facilitates an accelerated, protective rehabilitation protocol focused on early motion and quadriceps activation, thereby aiming to reduce failure rates and postoperative stiffness. This method represents a synergistic evolution in PCL reconstruction, combining synthetic reinforcement with biological healing.

title: Cartilage-targeting engineered probiotic bacterial extracellular vesicles treat osteoarthritis through modulation of matrix homeostasis.
abstract: Reversing extracellular matrix (ECM) metabolic dysregulation to facilitate cartilage repair represents a key therapeutic strategy for osteoarthritis (OA) treatment. Owing to the avascular nature of joint structures, intra-articular injection is a commonly used clinical administration route. However, the current drug retention time is insufficient to effectively reverse OA progression. In this study, we demonstrated that natural bacterial extracellular vesicles (BEVs) are capable of repairing cartilage damage. We modified Lactobacillus rhamnosus GG (LGG)-derived BEVs with a chondrocyte-targeting peptide to prolong their therapeutic efficacy. Engineered BEVs, as a drug delivery system, are capable of continuously transporting endogenous miRNAs. Cartilage-targeting LGG-EVs (W-LGG-EVs) penetrate deeply into cartilage tissue and promote extracellular matrix secretion by chondrocytes. Furthermore, W-LGG-EVs were shown to restore cartilage homeostasis and ultimately alleviate stress-related OA. BEVs, as a novel and safe therapeutic agent, hold clinical feasibility.

title: When Athletes Ask About Chronic Traumatic Encephalopathy.
abstract: Athletes exposed to repetitive head impacts (RHI) may seek clinical evaluation because of concerns about chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE), a neuropathologically defined disease that cannot currently be diagnosed during life. As public awareness of CTE has expanded, clinicians face challenges communicating diagnostic uncertainty, interpreting non-specific symptoms, and addressing concerns about future neurological health. This Current Opinion examines the widening gap between public expectations and scientific capability and considers its implications for athlete-centered care. We discuss how clinicians can acknowledge uncertainty without dismissing patients' concerns, identify potentially treatable contributors to symptoms without prematurely attributing them to neurodegenerative disease, and use shared decision-making to guide individualized evaluation and management. We also consider how concerns about CTE may influence decisions about continued participation and return-to-sport among current athletes. Meeting these challenges requires coordinated interdisciplinary care, evidence-based communication, and clinical approaches that prioritize meaningful intervention even when diagnostic certainty remains unavailable.

title: Flexible and stretchable bioelectronics for sports wearable monitoring: Materials, Device Engineering, and Intelligent Wearable Platforms.
abstract: Modern sports science is undergoing a paradigm shift from subjective coaching to objective, data-driven precision training. Consequently, wearable electronics for acquiring precise data during sports activities are attracting attention. However, conventional rigid wearables inherently suffer from mechanical mismatches between rigid wearables and the soft, deformable human skin, inducing severe motion artifacts and restricting natural biomechanics during high-intensity athletic activities. To address these limitations from a comprehensive perspective, this review systematically summarizes and analyzes recent advancements in next-generation flexible and stretchable bioelectronics tailored specifically for sports applications. We systematically examine the substrate materials, structural engineering designs, and device-level optimization strategies required to withstand repetitive strain, shear, and sweat-intensive environments. Building upon these conformable bio-interfaces, we discuss three core sensing modalities: electrochemical sensors for real-time analysis of sweat biomarkers, biophysical sensors for continuous electrophysiological and hemodynamic monitoring, and electromechanical sensors for high-fidelity kinematic and impact tracking. Furthermore, we discuss body-derived energy harvesting strategies to power sports wearables and wireless communication systems for continuous athletic monitoring. The importance of artificial intelligence and machine learning is increasing, as these techniques enable the removal of motion artifacts and facilitate objective analysis of athletic data for training and health monitoring applications. By evaluating targeted applications across aerobic and anaerobic exercise, cognitive state assessment, and post-exercise recovery, this review demonstrates how next-generation sports wearables contribute to the shift in sports science from reactive treatment toward proactive, data-driven performance enhancement and injury prevention.

title: Pre-season friendly match-play as a double-edged sword: Performance gains and inflammatory cost in semi-professional soccer players (a natural experiment).
abstract: Pre-season training prepares soccer players for competition, but the longitudinal effects of friendly match exposure remain unclear. We investigated whether cumulative late pre-season match-play is associated with physiological adaptation in semi-professional players. Twenty-four male players from a randomly selected semi-professional team competing at national level were assessed at pre-season start, mid-pre-season and pre-competition. Measurements included body composition, physical performance, aerobic fitness and blood markers reflecting muscle damage, inflammation, hormonal status and haematological adaptation. Based on cumulative playing time across eight friendly matches, as determined by coaching staff, players were classified retrospectively into extended play (EP) or limited play (LP) groups. Controlling for mid-pre-season baseline, the EP group showed significantly lower pre-competition values for body mass ( η p 2 = 0.276), body fat ( η p 2 = 0.294) and 35 m sprint time ( η p 2 = 0.129) and higher values for lower-limb power (dominant/non-dominant; η p 2 = 0.219-0.424), velocity at maximal oxygen uptake ( η p 2 = 0.441) and at second ventilatory threshold ( η p 2 = 0.708), serum glutamic-oxaloacetic transaminase ( η p 2 = 0.296), myoglobin ( η p 2 = 0.199), high-sensitivity C-reactive protein ( η p 2 = 0.920), interleukin-6 ( η p 2 = 0.893), tumour necrosis factor-α ( η p 2 = 0.937) and red blood cell count ( η p 2 = 0.190) (all P ≤ 0.038). Across all participants, total match-play time was correlated significantly with reductions in body fat (r = -0.47) and increases in lower-limb power (r = 0.44-0.67), second ventilatory threshold (r = 0.55) and inflammatory markers (r = 0.79-0.86) (all P ≤ 0.033). Greater friendly match-play exposure during pre-season was associated with favourable physiological adaptations and a more pronounced physiological and inflammatory response. These findings support friendly match-play as a meaningful physiological stimulus and highlight the importance of balancing match exposure with recovery during pre-season preparation.

title: Selective Electrical Muscle Stimulation of the Vastus Medialis in a Patient With Knee Osteoarthritis, With Changes in Muscle Quality, Symptoms, and Physical Activity: A Case Report.
abstract: BACKGROUND Fat accumulation in the vastus medialis has been associated with the progression of knee osteoarthritis. Electrical muscle stimulation may reduce intramuscular fat accumulation by inducing contractions of the targeted muscle. We hypothesized that electrical stimulation of the vastus medialis would be associated with a reduction in intramuscular fat and improvement in self-reported symptoms during the observation period in a patient with knee osteoarthritis. CASE REPORT The patient was a 77-year-old man with Kellgren-Lawrence grade 2 right knee osteoarthritis. Because he also had hypertension and hyperlipidemia, he had maintained regular exercise habits, including aquatic walking; however, he discontinued these activities because of knee pain. Electrical stimulation was applied to the vastus medialis for 30 minutes per session, 3 times per week, for 4 weeks. Ultrasound echo intensity, an indirect indicator of intramuscular fat, and the Knee Injury and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score were assessed before and after the intervention. Compared with the pre-intervention value, vastus medialis echo intensity decreased by 13.7 arbitrary units (25.3%), and knee symptoms improved during the observation period. He resumed aquatic walking 2 weeks after electrical stimulation was initiated. CONCLUSIONS During the observation period, vastus medialis echo intensity decreased, Knee Injury and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score scores improved, and he resumed aquatic walking. However, because this was a single uncontrolled case and physical activity resumed during the intervention, these changes cannot be attributed to electrical stimulation alone; spontaneous improvement, behavioral reactivation, or a combination of these factors remain plausible. Controlled studies across different levels of disease severity are needed.

title: Associations between countermovement jump impulse and running kinetics following ACL reconstruction.
abstract: Persistent deficits in lower-limb loading are commonly observed following anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction (ACLR) and may influence running biomechanics. Countermovement jump (CMJ) impulse can provide a phase-specific measure of force-time characteristics to reflect limb loading capacity; however, its relationship with running kinetics remains unclear. This study aimed to quantify phase-specific CMJ impulse following ACLR and examine associations with vertical ground reaction force (vGRF) metrics during treadmill running at the return-to-running phase. Forty-two participants performed three unilateral and bilateral CMJs on dual force plates and ran at 8 km/hr on an instrumented treadmill. Concentric, eccentric braking, and landing impulses were calculated. Running variables included weight acceptance rate, weight acceptance peak force, and maximum applied force. Inter-limb differences were assessed using Wilcoxon/paired t-tests. Impulse-vGRF relationships were analysed using Pearson/Spearman correlations and multiple linear regression. The ACLR limb exhibited significant deficits across all unilateral and bilateral CMJ phases, except for unilateral landing impulse. Deficits were greatest for unilateral concentric impulse (Δ1.3Ns·kg-0.67, d = 1.49, p < 0.001). Maximum applied force limb symmetry index (LSI) was explained by unilateral concentric impulse LSI (adjusted R2 = 0.25, p < 0.001). Maximum applied force of the affected limb was explained by unilateral concentric impulse (adjusted R2 = 0.38, p < 0.001). Weight acceptance peak force of the affected limb was explained by unilateral concentric and landing impulses (adjusted R2 = 0.37, p < 0.001). No meaningful relationships were observed for eccentric impulses or weight acceptance rate metrics. These findings indicate that jump impulse testing may provide clinically relevant indicators of running kinetics.

title: The "Minimizing Excessive Rotational Instability Technique" (MERI Technique): A Simple Lateral Tenodesis Reconstructing the Condylar Strap, the Distal Kaplan Fibers, and the Femoral Insertion of the Anterolateral Ligament to Control Internal Rotation During Anterior Cruciate Ligament Surgery.
abstract: The Minimizing Excessive Rotational Instability technique is a simple and minimally invasive lateral tenodesis designed to enhance internal rotation control during anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction by reconstructing the distal Kaplan fibers, the condylar strap, and the femoral insertion of the anterolateral ligament. Using a 1-cm-wide fascia lata strip, the procedure involves fixation with a single anchor at an isometric point proximal to the anterolateral ligament insertion, followed by a continuous locking suture and fascia lata closure on the anchor, which further reinforces rotational stability without excessive constraint. Although possibly biomechanically less restrictive than traditional lateral extra-articular tenodesis, the Minimizing Excessive Rotational Instability technique strikes a balance between stability and flexibility, potentially reducing postoperative stiffness and morbidity. Its simplicity, cost-effectiveness, and minimal invasiveness make it a valuable alternative for addressing anterolateral instability in select anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction patients.

title: Exosomes in regenerative medicine from biological messengers to engineered nanocarriers for precision therapeutics.
abstract: Exosomes have emerged as a promising class of next-generation nanocarriers at the intersection of regenerative medicine and drug delivery. Compared with conventional synthetic nanocarriers and stem cell-based therapies, exosomes offer unique advantages, including intrinsic biocompatibility, low immunogenicity, blood-barrier penetration, and natural intercellular cargo transfer. This review critically examines exosome biology, beginning with their biogenesis, structural composition, and roles in cellular homeostasis, immune regulation, autophagy, and tissue repair. Particular emphasis is placed on their therapeutic relevance in wound healing, neuroregeneration, cardiovascular repair, musculoskeletal regeneration, and cancer. The review further discusses major strategies for exosomal cargo engineering, including passive loading, electroporation, sonication, transfection-based approaches, extrusion, freeze-thaw treatment, and chemical functionalization. In addition, scaffold-assisted delivery systems and hybrid exosome-synthetic nanocarrier platforms are highlighted as important advances for improving local retention, targeting precision, and controlled release. Despite strong preclinical promise, translation remains limited by challenges in scalable manufacturing, purification, batch consistency, loading efficiency, potency assessment, and regulatory standardization. Future progress in this field will depend on the development of scalable and GMP-compatible exosome manufacturing, standardized purification and characterization methods, validated potency assays, regulatory-aligned quality control, and artificial intelligence (AI) engineering strategies to translate exosome-based platforms into safe, reproducible, and clinically effective regenerative therapeutics.

title: Immunomodulatory and Antioxidant Biomimetic Hydrogel Coloaded with Glycyrrhizic Acid and Copper Gallate for Synergistic Cartilage Regeneration.
abstract: Articular cartilage lesions are persistently restrained by three interwoven pathological drivers: chronic inflammatory response, sustained oxidative stress, and progressive extracellular matrix (ECM) catabolism. Coupled with the inherently weak self-repair capacity of hyaline cartilage, effective therapeutic interventions for such injuries remain an unmet clinical demand owing to the inherently poor self-repair capacity of hyaline cartilage, effective therapeutic interventions remain an unmet clinical demand. Herein, we engineered a biomimetic composite hydrogel designated ECM/HAMA/GA@Cu-GA, which integrates decellularized cartilage extracellular matrix, methacrylated hyaluronic acid (HAMA), glycyrrhizic acid (GA), and copper gallate (Cu-GA). This integrated hydrogel platform simultaneously endows biomimetic mechanical support, potent anti-inflammatory and antioxidative bioactivities, as well as robust chondrogenic induction capacity. In vitro cellular evaluations verified the outstanding biocompatibility of the composite hydrogel. The biomaterial efficiently polarizes macrophages toward the anti-inflammatory M2 phenotype, suppresses the secretion of pro-inflammatory mediators and matrix-degrading proteases, and facilitates the migration and chondrogenic differentiation of bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs). Transcriptomic profiling suggested that its underlying molecular mechanisms may involve activation of the PI3K/Akt signaling cascade and blockade of the NF-κB-mediated inflammatory pathway. In vivo assessments using rat articular cartilage defect models demonstrated that the ECM/HAMA/GA@Cu-GA hydrogel achieves satisfactory synchronous regeneration of hyaline cartilage and subchondral bone at 4 and 8 weeks post-implantation, with superior regenerative performance relative to all control groups. Collectively, this multifunctional hydrogel enables comprehensive remodeling of the pathological joint microenvironment with favorable biosafety profiles, representing a translatable candidate strategy for clinical management of cartilage degenerative disorders.

title: Gene amplification during differentiation of mesenchymal stem cells towards chondrocytes.
abstract: For decades, gene amplification was described as an attribute of tumor cells and as a physiological mechanism to increase gene copy numbers for the higher protein demand during the development of amphibians and flies. Notably, gene amplification has since been detected in normal mammalian cells during differentiation. Numerous amplified genes detected in tumor cells overlap with amplified genes detected during stem cell differentiation. Since stem cells have a valuable potency in regenerative therapies and since cartilage regeneration is a highly demanded therapeutic strategy, the current study investigated gene amplification dynamics during the chondrogenic differentiation of human mesenchymal stem cells (hMSCs). Using quantitative PCR, copy number changes were analyzed for genes previously implicated in differentiation, as well as genes amplified in chondrosarcoma, including CDK4, MDM2, AGAP2, CPT1B, SHANK3, TRIB1 and MYC. Amplifications were transient and stage-specific: CDK4, CPT1B and SHANK3 exhibited the highest copy number increases at day 2, followed by a gradual decline by day 7, whereas AGAP2 and MDM2 increased later in differentiation. Laser microdissection of toluidine blue-stained areas revealed heterogeneity in amplification patterns: CDK4 amplification was prominent in areas lacking or showing moderate proteoglycan deposition; CPT1B amplification occurred in regions with absent, moderate or intense proteoglycan deposition; and SHANK3 amplification was restricted to areas with intense proteoglycan deposition. Notably, regions with the strongest proteoglycan staining exhibited no gene amplification, suggesting that gene amplification is an early, transient event that diminishes as differentiation progresses. These findings highlight gene amplification as a mechanism during chondrogenesis, potentially critical for early differentiation stages and genome stability in mature cells.

title: PTHrP suppresses BMP2-induced osteochondral differentiation and preserves cartilage phenotype in mesenchymal stem cells via inactivating PI3K-AKT signaling.
abstract: Bone morphogenetic protein 2 (BMP2) has the potential to drive multipotent mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) to undergo chondral-osteogenic (including hypertrophic chondrocyte) differentiation. Parathyroid hormone-related protein (PTHrP) plays an essential role in fetal endochondral ossification, although persistent PTHrP stimulation leads to postnatal bone loss. Here, we investigated the effects of PTHrP on BMP2-induced endochondral ossification through hypertrophic chondrocyte differentiation of MSCs. We found that silencing PTHrP expression inhibited BMP2-induced chondrogenic, hypertrophic, and osteogenic differentiation of MSCs, while overexpression of PTHrP promoted BMP2-induced chondrogenic differentiation of MSCs and suppressed BMP2-induced hypertrophic differentiation of MSCs. Using stem cell implantation studies in athymic nude mice, we demonstrated that while MSCs with silenced PTHrP expression exhibited significantly reduced endochondral ossification of subcutaneous cartilage, overexpression of PTHrP promoted the growth of subcutaneous cartilage while significantly delaying ossification, leading to the preservation of cartilage phenotype. Mechanistically, we showed that exogenous PTHrP promoted BMP2-induced chondrogenic differentiation of MSCs by up-regulating Sox9 expression and inactivating PI3K-AKT signaling. Collectively, our findings strongly suggest that PTHrP may play an important role in mediating BMP2-induced chondral-osteogenic differentiation of MSCs by inactivating PI3K-AKT signaling, indicating that PTHrP may be exploited for endochondral cartilage-bone tissue engineering.

title: Ultrasound-triggered bio-scaffold integrating engineered stem cells for cartilage regeneration.
abstract: Articular cartilage repair remains a major clinical challenge due to the limited regenerative capacity of the tissue and the poor therapeutic efficacy of current treatments. Although stem cell-based therapies hold promise, their clinical outcomes are often compromised by insufficient chondrogenic differentiation, phenotypic instability, and rapid cell loss in the dynamic joint environment. Herein, we report an ultrasound-responsive, bio-scaffold system (e-BMSCs/Gel) designed to enhance cartilage regeneration through coordinated biochemical and genetic regulation. In this system, bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) are engineered by internalizing nanobubbles (NBs) loaded with TGF-β3 protein and CRISPR/Cas9 plasmids targeting the YAP (pCas9-YAP), termed T@NBspDNA. Additionally, to enhance cell retention and survival, engineered BMSCs (e-BMSCs) are encapsulated within a thermosensitive thiolated-chitosan/hydroxyapatite hydrogel that rapidly forms in situ. Under US stimulation, the synchronized activation of TGF-β3 release and YAP gene silencing significantly promoted the chondrogenic differentiation of e-BMSCs. Furthermore, in vivo evaluation in a rat articular cartilage defect model demonstrates that US-activated e-BMSCs/Gel effectively promotes hyaline-like cartilage regeneration and improves structural restoration of the defect site. Overall, this work presents a controllable bio-scaffold platform, offering a novel strategy for effective cartilage regeneration.

title: Targeting the lactate/P300/H3K18la epigenetic pathway with a mechanoadaptive biomimetic hydrogel to suppress traumatic tendon heterotopic ossification.
abstract: Traumatic heterotopic ossification (HO) is a debilitating complication of tendon injury, yet its pathogenic mechanisms remain elusive and effective preventive strategies are lacking. Here, we identify a glycometabolic-epigenetic axis that drives HO progression. Single-cell profiling and functional analyses reveal that hypoxic chondrocytes undergo glycolytic reprogramming, leading to lactate accumulation and transfer into tendon-derived mesenchymal stem cells (TD-MSCs) through MCT1. This metabolic coupling promotes P300-dependent histone H3 lysine 18 lactylation (H3K18la), activating osteogenic programs characterized by Col6a1, Zhx3, Lox and Vdr expression and thereby facilitating pathological endochondral ossification. Guided by this mechanism, we develop a tendon-adhesive hydrogel (GelHA-A485@Exos) that integrates mechanical repair with targeted epigenetic modulation. MSC-derived exosomes enable localized delivery of the P300 inhibitor A485, suppressing H3K18la and aberrant osteogenic activation, while the hydrogel scaffold enhances tendon regeneration. In vivo and in vitro studies demonstrate that GelHA-A485@Exos promotes tendon healing while preventing HO formation. Our findings establish metabolic-epigenetic communication as a central regulator of traumatic HO and provide a translational therapeutic strategy for its clinical prevention.

title: Sleep, Chronotype and Physiological Acclimatisation During a 21-Day Altitude Training Camp in World-Class Swimmers.
abstract: Altitude training is widely used in elite swimming, although its effects on sleep and acclimatisation remain insufficiently understood. The aim of this study was to describe changes in sleep difficulty, physiological acclimatisation, athlete-reported outcomes, and haematological markers during a 21-day altitude training camp (2320 m), and to explore the association between chronotype and sleep difficulty. Seven world-class swimmers (4 men, 3 women) were monitored before, during, and after altitude exposure. Sleep difficulty was assessed using the Athlete Sleep Screening Questionnaire, while daily monitoring included resting oxygen saturation, resting heart rate, acute mountain sickness symptoms, fatigue, recovery, hydration status, and training load. Chronotype was determined using the Morningness-Eveningness Questionnaire. Sleep difficulty was descriptively higher during the first week at altitude (6.14 ± 1.07 vs. 4.14 ± 1.21 at baseline) and returned towards baseline by week 3 (4.29 ± 1.50), although pairwise comparisons did not remain significant after multiplicity correction. Strong inverse associations between chronotype and sleep difficulty were observed at baseline (rho = -0.87, p = 0.014) and week 1 (rho = -0.85, p = 0.019), but neither met the Bonferroni-adjusted significance threshold (α = 0.010). SpO2 increased across the camp, with week 3 significantly higher than weeks 1 and 2 after Bonferroni correction, whereas RHR was significantly lower in week 3 than in week 1, but not week 2, after correction. Athlete-reported outcomes remained stable, acute mountain sickness symptoms were minimal, and haematological and iron-status markers showed no significant pre-to-post changes. Sleep difficulty showed a transient descriptive increase during the initial phase of the altitude camp, while SpO2 and RHR changes were consistent with physiological acclimatisation. Chronotype-related differences in sleep difficulty appeared to be present before altitude exposure rather than emerging specifically during the camp. Given the small sample size, these findings should be considered exploratory and hypothesis-generating.

title: Application of FTIR to detect changes in blood plasma during a pre-competition period in a professional heavyweight boxer.
abstract:
OBJECTIVES AND DESIGN: This exploratory single-case study examined whether repeated attenuated total reflectance Fourier transform infrared (ATR-FTIR) spectroscopy of blood plasma is technically feasible during a short pre-competition period and whether spectral regions co-vary with conventionally assayed biochemical markers.
METHODS: One professional heavyweight boxer was monitored over a 13-day pre-competition period characterized by reduced training load (tapering). Morning fasting blood was collected on five occasions (10, 13, 17, 20, and 23 May 2024) into lithium-heparin tubes and centrifuged to obtain plasma. Creatine kinase (CK), C-reactive protein (CRP), glucose, cortisol, testosterone, total and reduced glutathione, malondialdehyde, and zinc were quantified by conventional laboratory assays; ATR-FTIR spectra were acquired separately from the same plasma aliquots and were not used to quantify any of these analytes. Each plasma sample was measured eight times, yielding 40 spectra from five biological observations; the technical replicates are presented to illustrate within-sample visual consistency. Associations between the intensities of 22 spectral peaks and 12 biochemical variables were explored using Pearson correlation.
RESULTS: Plasma biochemical parameters showed changes during the pre-competition tapering period, including decreases in CK and CRP and increases in glutathione and testosterone, whereas cortisol remained relatively stable. FTIR spectra exhibited consistent vibrational profiles with changes in selected band intensities over time. Linear regression identified strong associations between glutathione levels and FTIR bands at 671, 699, and 721 cm-1 (R 2 = 0.80-0.92), as well as between cortisol and the 3,009 cm-1 band (R 2 = 0.77). Because of the limited number of observations (n = 5), these findings are preliminary and require validation in larger cohorts.
CONCLUSIONS: Repeated plasma measurements using ATR-FTIR demonstrated technical feasibility and visual consistency during a short pre-competition period in the studied athlete, while identifying potential spectral regions worthy of further investigation. The obtained results should be treated as preliminary. However, they do not provide evidence that ATR-FTIR enables the quantitative determination of glutathione or cortisol, or that it can be used to assess an athlete's competitive readiness. Confirmation of such capabilities requires studies involving adequately large and diverse groups of participants.

title: Osteoarthritis-Microenvironment-Triggered Phase Alteration of Injectable Conductive Hydrogel for Attenuating Cartilage Degradation.
abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is associated with excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS) production, which contributes substantially to chondrocyte dysfunction, oxidative stress, and cartilage degradation. Although stimuli-responsive hydrogels have emerged as promising platforms for OA therapy, conventional hydrogel-based systems exhibit limited sensitivity and require external detection equipment, highlighting the need for a simple, sensitive, and directly observable monitoring system. To address these challenges, we developed a ROS-triggered, in situ-forming gel-sol transition of a polydopamine (PDA)-loaded, diselenide-crosslinked polymer dot (PD) injectable hydrogel (HGC-PDA@PD or OA gel) as a monitorable theranostic for OA therapy at physiological temperature (37°C). The monitorable OA microenvironment-responsive hydrogel relied on interactions between the high ROS levels in OA cartilage and the OA gel, which triggered diselenide bond cleavage and the release of PDA from PD, causing a unique gel-sol transition of the OA gel. Owing to PDA release after diselenide breakage, the fluorescence and electroconductivity of the OA gel changed, which could serve as additional signals during OA detection. In vitro studies demonstrated the sensitive gel-sol transition of OA gel towards OA-induced immature articular chondrocytes (IL-1β/siSOD1/siCatalase-transfected iMACs). Furthermore, the OA gel showed a distinct gel-sol transition in cartilage of an in vivo OA mouse model compared with that in control mice. The lower transcription levels of cartilage matrix-degrading enzymes (ADAMTS4, ADAMTS5, MMP-3, and MMP-13) observed after OA gel injection confirmed that the OA gel could scavenge ROS and attenuate cartilage damage, revealing its potential application for dual-function OA diagnosis and rehabilitation.

title: Limb Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury in Rats is partially mediated by enhancing Necroptosis via Phosphorylation of RIPK1 and MLKL.
abstract: Limb ischemia-reperfusion injury (L-IRI) causes severe skeletal muscle damage and functional impairment through activation of regulated cell-death and inflammatory pathways. Necroptosis is a regulated form of necrotic cell death mediated through the receptor-interacting protein kinase 1 (RIPK1)-RIPK3-mixed lineage kinase domain-like protein (MLKL) signaling axis. Prior experimental studies have shown that Necrostatin-1 (Nec-1) attenuates acute skeletal muscle ischemia-reperfusion injury in rats. However, how Nec-1-sensitive protection relates to RIPK1/MLKL-associated signaling, circulating muscle injury markers, inflammatory responses, histological damage, and functional recovery during the early postischemic period remains incompletely defined. In this study, we used a rat model of unilateral hindlimb ischemia involving 3 hours of ischemia followed by reperfusion for up to 7 days to evaluate these interrelated responses. Nec-1 was administered before ischemia and after reperfusion. L-IRI resulted in elevated plasma creatine kinase and lactate dehydrogenase levels, severe histopathological injury, increased TUNEL staining, impaired grip strength, and reduced Modified Tarlov scores. These changes were accompanied by increased phosphorylation of RIPK1 and MLKL, activation of inflammatory signaling pathways, and altered expression of injury-associated inflammatory mediators. Nec-1 treatment reduced RIPK1/MLKL-associated signaling, inflammatory mediator expression, circulating muscle injury markers, and histological injury while preserving muscle architecture and improving functional recovery. These findings support and extend previous evidence that Nec-1-sensitive necroptosis-associated signaling contributes to early skeletal muscle injury following L-IRI. Pharmacologic targeting of regulated necrotic and inflammatory pathways warrants further investigation as a potential adjunct strategy for limiting acute skeletal muscle injury after limb reperfusion.

title: Supporting adolescent menstrual health to improve participation and performance in physical activity: rapid realist review to inform a logic model for intervention development.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Insufficient physical activity is higher in women and girls globally, with increased risk of non-communicable diseases. Menstrual (period-related) symptoms are a recognised barrier to adolescents engaging in physical activity. There is a lack of evidence-based guidance to address this barrier.
OBJECTIVE: To develop a set of initial programme theories (context-mechanism-outcome configurations, CMOCs) to describe how existing menstrual health support interventions work, for whom, how and in what circumstances to inform a logic model for intervention development.
DESIGN: Rapid realist review.
METHODS: Formal, double-screened, database (Medline, AMED, Embase, Psycinfo, CINAHL, ERIC, SCOPUS; June 2025) and grey literature searches guided by stakeholder expertise. Articles were selected that met inclusion criteria and contributed to theory development. Explanatory statements were extracted and synthesised into CMOCs using Pawson’s reasoning processes and mapped onto Self-Determination Theory concepts (autonomy, competency, relatedness).
RESULTS: From 9585 database hits, 63 articles were included. Three generated initial programme theories describe how four identified intervention domains (education; practicalities including toilet facilities, clothing and free accessible period products; menstrual cycle tracking and screening tools; and medical support if needed) could improve menstrual health confidence and understanding (M), communication and trust (M)—to empower individuals to enhance their own menstrual health (M) and potentially improve participation rates and performance in physical activity (O). Alternative causal pathways describe potential adverse outcomes when processes are not in place to: signpost to medical support if needed (M), support user trust in how and why data are collected and used (M) and enable understanding of the limitations of menstrual health support tools (M). Contextual data are needed to further refine these theories that are presented as a logic model.
CONCLUSION: The proposed logic model can be used to inform and evaluate future interventions aimed at overcoming menstrual health related barriers with physical activity.

title: EMSCs-derived exosomes rescue p75NTR-/- -mediated osteogenesis deficiency via PI3K/Akt/ERK1/2 signaling pathways.
abstract: The repair of the critical-sized bone defects remains a major challenge for orthopedic surgeons, particularly when osteogenesis is impaired by p75 neurotrophin receptor (p75NTR) deficiency. However, the underlying molecular mechanisms are not fully understood. This study aimed to clarify the role of p75NTR in bone regeneration and to develop a cell-free approach to rescue p75NTR-/- deficiency-mediated osteogenic deficiency through a controlled releasing of wild-type ectomesenchymal stem cells exosomes (WT-Exo) which were incorporated into silk fibroin/polycaprolactone2:5/polyvinyl alcohol (SF/PCL2:5/PVA) coaxial nanofibrous membranes. p75NTR-/- mice exhibited a reduced bone mass and delayed ossification, while WT-Exo-loaded membranes partially restored osteogenic deficiency in p75NTR-/- cells and enhanced expression of osteogenic markers such as alkaline phosphatase (ALP), collagen type I (Col-I), osteopontin (OPN) and runt-related transcription factor 2 (Runx2) aaccompanied by activating of phosphoinositide 3-kinase (PI3K)/protein kinase B (Akt)/extracellular signal-regulated kinase 1/2 (ERK1/2) signaling pathway. Following implantation of the WT-Exo-loaded membranes into the critical-sized cranial defects in p75NTR-/- mice, new bone formation in the defect site was significantly improved by a sustained release of WT-Exo. Overall, the findings in this study highlighted the critical role of p75NTR in osteogenic differentiation of ectomesenchymal stem cells (EMSCs) and demonstrated that WT-Exo, delivered via the coaxial electrospun membranes, represented an effective cell-free intervention method to reverse bone formation deficiency caused by p75NTR deficiency, providing a promising strategy for gene deficiency-related bone diseases.

title: Advancing regenerative biomaterials and translational strategies in orthopaedic traumatology.
abstract: The 2025 Orthopaedic Trauma Association's Basic Science Focus Forum featured a symposium on regenerative biomaterials and translational strategies for orthopaedic trauma. Four experts presented complementary perspectives on the next generation of bone and soft tissue repair: Dr. J. Tracy Watson described how orthobiologics and refined spacer design can be used to engineer a better Masquelet induced membrane; Dr. Lauren Priddy presented evidence that hydroxyapatite coatings can mitigate the rapid degradation of additively manufactured magnesium scaffolds; Dr. Vaida Glatt described the development and clinical translation of the Biomimetic Hematoma scaffold for bone and muscle regeneration; and Dr. Katherine Hixon outlined how the 3R principles (Replacement, Reduction, Refinement) can serve as a framework to accelerate musculoskeletal regenerative engineering. Collectively, the symposium underscored a shift toward biologically informed, clinically predictive, and ethically responsible engineering solutions for the patients who sustain musculoskeletal trauma.

title: Young Investigator Award: Where Do We Start? A Conceptual Model for Implementing Menstrual Cycle Tracking in Sport.
abstract: Menstrual cycle tracking is a much-discussed component of the ' female athlete' research theme; however, more translational work is needed to meet practitioners' desire for further guidance on the implementation of tracking in applied settings. The purpose of this paper is to present a preliminary conceptual model to inform practitioners' decision-making around menstrual cycle tracking and assist researchers in identifying and framing future research directions. The proposed model-Conducting and Navigating menstrual cycle Education, Communication and Tracking (ConNECT)-proposes that communication and education strategies may be utilised to affect social, organisational and individual level change, ultimately supporting the implementation of menstrual cycle tracking by increasing its uptake and impact. This model was developed based on the findings from a series of studies conducted by the authors, which considered the existing literature on tracking and the perspectives of athletes and practitioners. Therefore, the ConNECT model offers an ecologically sound starting point for sport scientists, coaches and other members of an athlete's support team to base their practice on.

title: Baseline Symptom Collection in Elite Rugby Union Players-Limited Clinical Utility? An Investigation of Assessments Across 5879 men and Women Athletes.
abstract: In World Rugby's Head Injury Assessment (HIA) protocol, a modified Sports Concussion Assessment Tool (SCAT) is completed during the pre-season (baseline) and when a player has a suspected head injury. The symptom component of the SCAT, which involves comparing current to baseline symptoms, has been shown to be the most predictive component for concussion diagnosis. Because the clinical comparison of symptom report to baseline is a key determinant of concussion diagnosis, this study aims to explore the relationship between symptoms endorsement at baseline and during HIA. Mean and standard deviation (SD) or median and interquartile ranges (IQR) are presented along with relevant bivariate analyses. Logistic regressions compared proportions of symptom endorsement profiles between men and women. At baseline, 'Trouble sleeping' and 'Fatigue or low energy' were commonly reported symptoms for men and women. At baseline, women (mean + SD) reported more symptoms than men (mean + SD) on average. During the HIA, women players were nearly 3 times (Relative risk: 2.98 95% CIs: 2.47-3.60) more likely than men to report fewer symptoms immediately after the match than at baseline (47% women vs. 16% men). While this study highlights the importance of collecting baseline assessment as a medical overview of players, it de-emphasises the relevance of baseline symptoms when using the SCAT as a clinical assessment tool in professional rugby players. This study also highlights important differences in men and women's rugby players in symptom reporting, and recommends de-coupling baseline symptom reporting from the diagnostic part of the HIA.

title: Tunable Polycaprolactone-Gelatin Methacryloyl Composites for Fused Deposition Modeling Musculoskeletal Scaffold Fabrication.
abstract: The global musculoskeletal burden continues to outpace standard of care transplantation efforts and existing tissue engineering solutions, necessitating further development of scalable biomaterials. In this study, we introduce a novel synthesis of polycaprolactone-gelatin methacryloyl (PCL-GelMA) composite filament, compatible with standard fused deposition modeling (FDM) 3D printers, for scalable and customizable scaffold fabrication. By incorporating 15% and 30% (w/w) GelMA into a PCL matrix, we achieved tunable modulation of surface roughness, hydrophilicity, and degradation kinetics. Mechanical testing revealed nonlinear dependencies between GelMA content and tensile properties, suggesting that variation in GelMA particle size and distribution leads to a concentration-dependent trade-off between stiffness and structural integrity. Human mesenchymal stem cells (hMSCs) cultured on printed scaffolds maintained viability and proliferative capacity. By mitigating solvent toxicity through upstream processing, physically integrating constituents into a unified bulk matrix, and leveraging the accessibility of FDM printing, this material platform enables scalable translation and further biomaterial exploration.

title: Tissue-Specific Regulation of Glucose and Lipid Metabolism by miR-29a in Insulin Resistance and Type 2 Diabetes.
abstract: MicroRNA-29a (miR-29a) has emerged as a context-dependent regulator of glucose and lipid metabolism in insulin-sensitive tissues, yet its tissue-specific actions in insulin resistance and type 2 diabetes remain incompletely understood. We synthesized peer-reviewed evidence retrieved from PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and EBSCOhost on the role of miR-29a across skeletal muscle, adipose tissue, liver, and pancreatic β-cells. We first define the nomenclature and genomic organization of the miR-29 family, its upstream transcriptional regulators, and the Argonaute-based evidence that separates direct target repression from correlative association. Across these tissues, miR-29a modulates oxidative metabolism, inflammatory signaling, and mitochondrial adaptation, largely through the PPARδ/PGC-1α axis, exerting complex and sometimes opposing effects depending on the tissue environment. We further examine miR-29a as a mediator of interorgan communication through extracellular vesicles, its responsiveness to exercise, and its emerging value as a biomarker and therapeutic target, while highlighting unresolved contradictions and translational hurdles. Because miR-29 family members act as tumor suppressors in most epithelial tissues, we also address the oncogenic risk inherent in nucleic acid strategies that lower miR-29a levels. Collectively, this mini-review positions miR-29a as a physiology-oriented integrator of metabolic remodeling and tissue-specific adaptation in metabolic disease.

title: Restoring the repair-fibrosis balance via a localized extracellular vesicle-pirfenidone dual-delivery biomaterial platform promotes ureteral repair after thermal injury.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Ureteral thermal injury can lead to ureteral stricture through persistent oxidative stress, inflammation, impaired vascular repair, and excessive fibrosis. Current treatment strategies primarily aim to restore urinary drainage or address established structural obstruction, whereas approaches that simultaneously modulate tissue repair and postinjury fibrotic remodeling remain limited.
OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to develop a localized dual-delivery biomaterial platform that simultaneously promotes tissue repair and suppresses excessive fibrosis after ureteral thermal injury.
METHODS: A localized EG_PFM platform was fabricated by combining a mesenchymal stem cell-derived extracellular vesicle (MSC-EV)-loaded chitosan/hyaluronic acid hydrogel (EG) with a pirfenidone (PF)-loaded poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid) nanofibrous membrane (PFM). The physicochemical properties and release profiles were characterized. In vitro, the effects of MSC-EVs and PF on urothelial and smooth muscle cell relative cell growth and migration, oxidative stress, angiogenesis, macrophage phenotype, and fibrosis-associated cellular responses were evaluated. A rabbit model of ureteral thermal injury was established to assess ureteral structural repair, hydronephrosis, collagen deposition, oxidative stress, inflammation, angiogenesis, and transcriptomic changes.
RESULTS: EG_PFM exhibited favorable biocompatibility, tissue adhesion, and sustained release of MSC-EVs and PF. MSC-EVs increased relative cell growth and enhanced the migration of urothelial and smooth muscle cells, reduced intracellular reactive oxygen species, enhanced endothelial tube formation and were associated with an M2-like macrophage phenotype, whereas PF suppressed α-SMA expression and extracellular matrix accumulation. In rabbits, EG_PFM reduced hydronephrosis and ureteral stricture, decreased collagen deposition, oxidative stress, and inflammatory responses, and enhanced vascularization. Transcriptomic analysis identified treatment-associated changes in multiple signaling and metabolic pathways, including calcium signaling, cell adhesion molecules, tyrosine metabolism, and retinol metabolism.
CONCLUSION: Localized codelivery of MSC-EVs and PF promoted reparative responses while limiting fibrotic remodeling, thereby improving structural repair after ureteral thermal injury. EG_PFM represents a promising localized therapeutic strategy for reducing postinjury ureteral stricture.

title: Nano-Armor Empowers Mesenchymal Stem Cells to Actively Target and Reverse Synovial Inflammation in Rheumatoid Arthritis.
abstract: Mesenchymal stem cell (MSC) therapy for rheumatoid arthritis (RA) remains hindered by the oxidative-induced pro-inflammatory synovial microenvironment, which largely impairs MSC homing, survival, and immunomodulatory function. Although nanomaterial modification holds promise for enhancing MSC therapeutic efficacy, conventional intracellular modification approaches carry risks of cytotoxicity and unpredictable stem cell fate alteration. Here, we empower MSCs with a surface-anchored, multifunctional RGD-MXene/MnO₂ nano-armor (RMM). MXene, with its large specific surface area, supports the in-situ growth of MnO₂ nanozymes and conjugation of RGD targeting peptides, while enabling stable covalent anchoring onto the MSC membrane via click chemistry. The RMM-armored MSCs exhibit robust protection against ROS-induced damage and fully restored immunomodulatory capacity due to the cascade catalase- and superoxide dismutase-like activities of MnO2, efficiently promoting macrophage polarization from pro-inflammatory M1 type to anti-inflammatory M2 type. In RA mouse models, the RGD peptide facilitates active MSC homing to inflamed synovial tissues by specifically recognizing integrin αvβ3. Thus, RMM@MSCs not only alleviate synovial inflammation but also prevent bone destruction and cartilage erosion, achieving highly efficient RA therapy with only one dose. This surface modification strategy resolves the long-standing translational barriers of conventional MSC therapy, providing a versatile and translatable platform for treating RA and other inflammatory diseases. STATEMENT OF SIGNIFICANCE: Although mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) are promising for rheumatoid arthritis (RA) due to their inherent immunomodulatory properties, their translation is hindered by poor homing to inflammatory joints and ROS-induced functional impairment. This work reports the use of a multifunctional RGD-MXene/MnO2 (RMM) nano-armor to enhance MSC therapy in RA. Specifically, MXene provides a large specific surface area for the in-situ growth of MnO2 nanoenzyme and the peptide conjugation, as well as the covalent anchoring on MSCs (favoring safe surface modification); MnO2's cascade enzyme-like activity establishes an antioxidant shield to reverse ROS-induced MSC apoptosis and exhaustion (maintaining MSC viability and biofunctions); RGD peptide targets highly expressed integrin αvβ3 in synovial pannus (enabling active MSC homing). Thus, the nano-armor-modified RMM@MSCs significantly inhibits synovitis, alleviates symptoms, and mitigates joint destruction.

title: DNA-adsorbing nanozyme hydrogel reprograms the immuno-oxidative microenvironment to support stem cell-based cartilage repair in osteoarthritis.
abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is a prevalent degenerative joint disease, and stem cell therapy is often limited by a hostile joint microenvironment. Excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS) and damage-associated cell-free DNA (cfDNA) cooperatively drive innate immune activation, inflammatory macrophage polarization, and chondrogenic instability, forming an immuno-oxidative barrier to cartilage repair. Here, we developed a bioactive DNA-adsorbing nanozyme hydrogel (MNKB/HA) to remodel this niche and enhance BMSC-mediated cartilage repair. MNKB/HA integrates Mn3O4 nanozymes with Kartogenin (KGN)-engineered bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) in an injectable hyaluronic acid matrix. Mn3O4 exhibited SOD- and CAT-like activities, scavenging O2·-, H2O2, and ·OH, while efficiently adsorbing cfDNA and CpG-ODN to suppress TLR9/MyD88 signaling and M1 polarization and promote M2 polarization. In vitro, 10 μg/mL Mn3O4 was cytocompatible, protected BMSCs and chondrocytes from H2O2-induced apoptosis, and reshaped inflammatory secretion, with IL-10 increased 8.3-fold and TNF-α, IL-6, and IL-1β reduced. KGN stabilized the chondrogenic phenotype (SOX9, COL Ⅱ, ACAN), while its combination with Mn3O4 synergistically enhanced chondrogenic stability under oxidative/inflammatory stress. In rat OA, intra-articular MNKB/HA reduced OARSI scores, restored COL II and ACAN, decreased MMP13, improved subchondral bone microarchitecture, and attenuated synovitis and osteophytes. MNKB/HA also reduced synovial cfDNA, weakened TLR9 signaling, promoted M2 polarization, and showed intra-articular retention for at least 10 days without notable systemic toxicity. Thus, MNKB/HA remodels the immuno-oxidative niche through synergistic ROS scavenging and cfDNA adsorption, providing a strategy for stem cell-mediated cartilage repair in OA.

title: M4-like Macrophages Drive Skeletal Muscle Fibrosis and Suppress Myogenesis via the MMP12/SPP1/NF-κB Axis.
abstract: Acute skeletal muscle repair depends on a finely tuned balance between myogenic regeneration and fibrotic remodeling. Macrophages are essential to this process, and specific subsets have been linked to fibrosis in some organs. The M4-like macrophage, a distinct polarization subset implicated in fibrotic diseases, has not been well characterized in the context of injured muscle, particularly regarding its impact on fibroblast activation and myogenic suppression. The study aims to explore the effects of M4-like macrophages in the repair of muscle injury and possible mechanism. We analyzed a murine single-cell RNA-sequencing dataset from cardiotoxin (CTX)-injured skeletal muscle to identify injury-expanded macrophage subsets and their molecular programs. Immunohistochemistry and immunofluorescence staining of muscle sections were used to assess CXCL4 expression and platelet (CD41+) infiltration in injured versus uninjured tissues. CXCL4-induced M4-like macrophages were established as an in vitro model to examine their effects on L929 fibroblasts and C2C12 myoblasts. The MMP12-SPP1 interaction was predicted by AlphaFold3 and validated by co-immunoprecipitation and immunofluorescence colocalization. Loss-of-function and rescue experiments targeting MMP12 and SPP1 were performed to determine their causal roles in fibroblast activation and myogenic suppression. Transcriptomic and biochemical analyses were used to define downstream macrophage-intrinsic NF-κB/TNF-α signaling. Finally, AAV-mediated macrophage-targeted SPP1 knockdown and pharmacological NF-κB inhibition were evaluated in the CTX injury model. Using a BALB/c mouse model of cardiotoxin (CTX)-induced acute skeletal muscle injury and a publicly available murine scRNA-seq dataset from CTX-injured skeletal muscle, we observed an injury-induced MMP12/SPP1-positive macrophage subset with an M4-like transcriptional signature. Mechanistically, co-immunoprecipitation assays and immunofluorescence colocalization supported an association between MMP12 and SPP1. MMP12 knockdown attenuated the pro-fibrotic and anti-myogenic effects of M4-like macrophages, whereas recombinant SPP1 largely restored these phenotypes. Furthermore, transcriptomic and biochemical analyses revealed that autocrine SPP1 activated NF-κB signaling in M4-like macrophages, and increased TNF-α secretion. Pharmacological inhibition of NF-κB signaling with QNZ reduced fibroblast activation and restored the expression of myogenic markers. However, QNZ is not TNF-α specific and may affect multiple cell types. In vivo, AAV-mediated macrophage-targeted SPP1 knockdown driven by the F4/80 promoter, as well as QNZ treatment in the CTX-induced muscle injury model, markedly decreased collagen deposition, enhanced myogenic regeneration, and improved functional recovery. These findings identify an MMP12/SPP1/NF-κB signaling pathway in M4-like macrophages, with TNF-α as a potential downstream mediator, that may contribute to an imbalance between regeneration and fibrosis and may represent a therapeutic target for enhancing skeletal muscle repair after acute injury.

title: Effects of Intramuscular Mesenchymal Stem Cell and Boric Acid Administration on Muscle Damage and Recovery in an Exhaustive Swimming Rat Model.
abstract: Exhaustive exercise induces damage to skeletal muscle, reducing athletic performance and delaying recovery. Effective experimental strategies are needed to mitigate this damage and accelerate tissue regeneration. This study aimed to address limitations in the therapeutic efficacy of bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stromal/stem cell-like cells (MSCs) associated with limited cell viability by evaluating boric acid (BA) as an antioxidant and metabolic modulator to enhance cell viability and muscle repair. Twenty-five female Wistar albino rats underwent a 15 day exhaustive swimming protocol and received intramuscular injections of MSCs (1 × 106 cells), BA (10 µg), or their combination, according to the experimental group allocation. Bone marrow obtained from five additional donor rats was used exclusively for MSC isolation and culture. Daily exhaustion time, serum biomarkers lactate, lactate dehydrogenase (LDH), creatine kinase (CK), and gastrocnemius histology were evaluated. Intramuscular BA improved endurance and reduced biochemical markers of muscle injury, whereas MSC application promoted structural muscle regeneration, as evidenced by centrally located nuclei and improved muscle fiber integrity. Combined MSCs + BA treatment improved several biochemical and histological outcomes compared with exercise alone. Serum lactate concentrations remained elevated in treated groups 24 h after the final exercise session, indicating altered post-exercise metabolic responses. Overall, intramuscular BA modulated metabolic responses, whereas administration of bone marrow-derived stromal/stem cell-like cells was associated with structural regeneration in this rat model of exercise-induced skeletal muscle injury, providing a reproducible platform for evaluating regenerative interventions.

title: Strontium- and magnesium-doped hydroxyapatite scaffolds enhance bone regeneration by promoting macrophage polarization toward the M2 phenotype.
abstract: The development of synthetic bone grafts that integrate osteogenic and immunomodulatory functions represents a critical strategy in regenerative orthopedics. In this study, we fabricated strontium- and magnesium-doped hydroxyapatite (HA/Mg/Sr) scaffolds derived from natural bovine cancellous bone. Physicochemical characterization confirmed the preservation of a three-dimensional interconnected porous architecture (∼80% porosity, ∼350 μm pore size) with a homogeneous nanoparticulate surface. Doping with Mg and Sr enhanced scaffold degradation, sustained the release of bioactive ions (,,), and significantly increased compressive strength to levels comparable with human cancellous bone.In vitro, HA/Mg/Sr scaffolds exhibited excellent biocompatibility, promoting adhesion and proliferation of both bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) and bone marrow-derived macrophages (BMMs). While Mg primarily facilitated direct osteogenic differentiation of BMSCs, Sr played a dominant role in directing macrophage polarization toward the anti-inflammatory M2 phenotype, as evidenced by increased CD206 and IL-10 expression alongside reduced CCR7 and pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-1β, IL-6, TNF-α). Notably, macrophage-conditioned medium from HA/Mg/Sr cultures substantially enhanced BMSC osteogenesis, highlighting immunomodulation as a central mechanism. Transcriptomic analysis indicated that the HA/Mg/Sr scaffolds promoted macrophage polarization toward the M2 phenotype and modulated immune responses potentially through the NF-κB signaling pathway, which was validated by Western blot. In a rat femoral condyle defect model, HA/Mg/Sr scaffolds-particularly those with 10% Sr content (HA/Mg/Sr2)-demonstrated superior bone regeneration, characterized by bone volume fraction (BV/TV), trabecular thickness (Tb.Th), trabecular number (Tb.N) and enhanced new bone ingrowth and integration, accompanied by elevated M2 macrophage infiltrationin vivo. Overall, these findings establish that HA/Mg/Sr scaffolds promote bone repair not only via direct osteoconduction but, more importantly, through immunomodulation-fostering a pro-healing M2 macrophage microenvironment potentially in an NF-κB-dependent manner, thereby offering a promising dual-functional biomaterial strategy for critical-sized bone defect reconstruction. Collectively, this study underscores the therapeutic relevance of targeting macrophage polarization in bone repair and delineates a mechanistic framework for Sr-based immunomodulatory biomaterial design.

title: Superiority of Tetrapeptide Tyr-Gly-Leu-Phe over Amino Acid Mixture: Mechanisms Underlying Enhanced Systemic Amino Acid Delivery, Anti-Fatigue Efficacy, and Muscle Damage Repair.
abstract: This study compared the anti-fatigue tetrapeptide YGLF with an equimolar amino acid (AA) mixture across three stages: postingestion absorption, postexercise fatigue, and muscle damage repair. Despite rapid in vitro degradation (<1% intact), YGLF elevated plasma AAs more effectively than the AA mixture 15 min postingestion (51.97 vs 46.34 mg/100 mL). Postexercise, YGLF outperformed the AA mixture by further increasing muscle AAs and blood glucose, reducing metabolic byproducts, and activating AMPK. Following muscle damage, transcriptomics revealed that the AA mixture primarily modulated energy metabolism, whereas YGLF uniquely upregulated muscle growth genes. Western blotting confirmed that YGLF promoted repair via the Sestrin2/mTOR and Pax7/MYOD pathways. These findings demonstrate the distinct bioactivity of YGLF over that of free AAs, establishing a rationale for utilizing specific peptides in sports nutrition and muscle recovery.

title: Delphinidin induces the upregulation of miR-23a-3p expression in skeletal muscle and miR-23a-3p release from intestinal cells.
abstract: Delphinidin, one of the major anthocyanidins, inhibits disuse muscle atrophy by increasing the expression of miR-23a-3p in mouse skeletal muscle. However, delphinidin is less stable and poorly absorbed in vivo, so its mechanism of function remains unclear. In this study, we aimed to elucidate the mechanism by which delphinidin increases miR-23a-3p expression in skeletal muscle. miRNAs can be packaged into extracellular vesicles (EVs) and secreted from cells. We investigated whether delphinidin induces the release of miR-23a-3p encapsulated in EVs from intestinal cells and whether these EVs increase miR-23a-3p expression in skeletal muscle cells. A single dose of delphinidin increased the expression of miR-23a-3p in the small intestine of mice. To examine whether delphinidin affects the secretion of miR-23a-3p in intestinal cells, we used differentiated Caco-2 cells as an in vitro model. Results showed that delphinidin increases the expression of miR-23a-3p in EVs secreted from differentiated Caco-2 cells. In addition, EVs derived from delphinidin-treated Caco-2 cells were taken up by differentiated C2C12 myotubes, resulting in increased intracellular miR-23a-3p expression. Our in vitro results suggest that intestinal cell-derived EVs may contribute to the antimuscle atrophy activity of delphinidin through the delivery of miR-23a-3p to skeletal muscle cells.

title: Binding of a Novel 11β-Hydroxysteroid to the Apelin Receptor (APLNR) and Its Possible Role in Regulating Skeletal Muscle Health in Mice.
abstract: Several molecules have been investigated for their potential to improve muscle health in models of muscle damage simulating sarcopenia, injury, or aging. Some small molecules induced beneficial effects on skeletal muscle by stimulating the apelin receptor (APLNR). This receptor has emerged as a promising pharmacological target for modulating muscle homeostasis. Using an in silico approach, we recently identified 11β-hydroxypregnenolone (11β-OHP5) as a potential skeletal muscle (SKM) modulator. We hypothesized that 11β-OHP5 interacts with and activates APLNR. This study employed several research approaches: (1) in silico molecular docking and molecular dynamics to explore the feasibility of 11β-OHP5 interacting with APLNR; (2) in vitro activation analysis to APLNR; (3) in vitro analysis C2C12 myoblast differentiation; (4) analysis of the molecule's presence in mouse skeletal muscle and its differential presence between young and older mice. The results show that 11β-OHP5, acting through APLNR, positively affects myoblast differentiation and may participate in the exercise-induced benefits in aging mice. We show that 11β-OHP5 interacts with APLNR, induces myogenic responses, is found in SKM; its concentration decreases with age, and exercise restores it. More work is necessary to understand the physiology of this possible endogenous molecule.

title: Aerobic Exercise Ameliorates Osteoarthritic Chondrocyte Degradation in Osteoarthritis via Regulating E2F8/NLRP14 Signaling Pathway.
abstract: Although physical activity is known to mitigate disease risks, its protective molecular mechanisms remain poorly understood. E2F8, a regulator of cell cycle and metabolism, showed significant differential expression between osteoarthritis (OA) and exercise models, suggesting it may link mechanical activity to OA alleviation. In vitro, Interleukin-1 Beta (IL-1β) simulated inflammation. In vivo, OA was induced in rats via Monosodium iodoacetate (MIA) injection. The effects of E2F8 and mechanical stress were assessed using moderate treadmill exercise, histology, and joint observation. Bioinformatic analysis, cyclic tensile strain, Western blot, immunofluorescence, and gene knockdown were used to investigate mechanisms. In OA rats, E2F8 was downregulated in cartilage while NLRP14 increased. Exercise reversed E2F8 downregulation, alleviated cartilage degeneration, restored anabolic activity, and reduced inflammatory catabolism linked to senescence. In vitro, mechanical stress reversed the IL-1β-induced anabolic/catabolic imbalance by regulating the E2F8/NLRP14, mitigating OA progression. Mechanical stress enhances E2F8 expression in osteoarthritic chondrocytes, which in turn protects cartilage by suppressing the expression of NLRP14. These findings underscore the role of E2F8 as a mechano-sensitive mediator and highlight the potential of exercise or exercise-mimetic therapies as effective strategies for preventing and treating OA.

title: Laser-programmed anisotropic hierarchical host bone interfaces for mechanotransduction-guided osseointegration.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Conventional mechanical osteotomy often induces thermal and mechanical damage, which compromises the biological quality of the host bone interface and impairs subsequent osseointegration. This study aimed to develop a 9.3 μm CO2 laser-based osteotomy strategy that integrates precise bone cutting with in situ regenerative interface engineering.
METHODS: A 9.3 μm CO2 laser osteotomy platform was developed by combining controlled pulse-overlap scanning with gas-atomized water-mist cooling. The generated osteotomy interfaces were characterized in terms of surface topography, thermal response, microstructural preservation, and local mechanical integrity. Human mesenchymal stem cell (hMSC) alignment, focal adhesion-mediated mechanotransduction, osteogenic differentiation, and osteoclast formation were evaluated in vitro. Transcriptomic and biochemical analyses were performed to investigate the underlying molecular programs. The optimized interface was further assessed in a rat femoral defect model with porous titanium scaffold implantation.
RESULTS: The laser osteotomy strategy generated deterministic microscale grooves and graded nanoscale roughness, forming anisotropic hierarchical micro-nano osteotomy interfaces. Compared with mechanical cutting, laser osteotomy reduced thermal accumulation, limited microstructural disruption, and better maintained local mechanical integrity. The engineered interfaces directed hMSC alignment and activated focal adhesion-mediated mechanotransduction, as indicated by enhanced pFAK activation, Lamin A/C reinforcement, and YAP nuclear translocation. These responses promoted osteogenic differentiation and suppressed osteoclast formation, with the Laser III group showing the most favorable biological response. Transcriptomic and biochemical analyses further revealed enrichment of adhesion-, cytoskeleton-, and PI3K-Akt-related osteogenic programs. In vivo, the optimized interface enhanced peri-implant bone regeneration, mineral apposition, and osseointegration.
CONCLUSIONS: This study provides proof-of-concept evidence that 9.3 μm CO2 laser osteotomy may enable bone cutting to be coupled with in situ regenerative interface engineering. By reducing cutting-associated damage and actively programming the host bone interface, this approach shows translational potential for improving peri-implant bone healing and implant integration.
THE TRANSLATIONAL POTENTIAL OF THIS ARTICLE: 9.3 μm CO2 laser-enabled osteotomy interface engineering integrates precise bone cutting with in situ programming of the host bone surface. This study reveals that laser-generated anisotropic hierarchical micro-nano interfaces can reduce cutting-associated damage, activate adhesion-mediated mechanotransduction, promote osteogenic differentiation, suppress osteoclast maturation, and enhance peri-implant osseointegration. These findings provide a regenerative osteotomy strategy for improving the biological quality of surgically created bone interfaces, which holds translational potential for orthopedic implant surgery, fracture reconstruction, and the repair of bone defects in clinical practice.
